text: {"score":2,"justification":"Most figures match the card, but the narrative adds unsupported claims and weak or contradictory inferences, and the next steps do not fit the findings. The headline and rationale start well with the 24.4% 99215 share, expected 1.9%, and 78% on 0-1 condition patients. Then the interpretation goes wrong.","problems":["Claims that the 'notes may have been inflated to match the bills' is speculation with no basis in the packet. All 14 documented 99215s supported the billed level, and the 7 of 26 no-lab figure is not shown to indicate inflation.","The '27% rate' is the ratio 7/26. It is an inference, but it is presented as a rate of notes that 'the claims do not show' and used to suggest inflation. The no-lab-on-claim gap has no benchmark and may be benign.","The summary describes 'the first response lacked signatures; the follow-up produced 30 usable charts', which does not appear in the evidence card. This looks fabricated.","Leaning is 'inconclusive' and the next steps say 'what came back is too thin to judge', yet 30 charts (12.4%) came back and all 14 99215 charts supported the level. This contradicts the framing and the headline, which says charts support 99215.","The next steps are generic ('request a larger sample', 're-screen'). They do not request documentation for the specific cited low-complexity 99215 claims, such as C0034539 and C0034546. They also do not tell the coder which notes to check, even though the text mentions a coder review.","The cited 99214 examples (C0034671, C0034749) are under-coded cases, which do not support the upcoding concern or the inflation point. Only two low-complexity 99215 claims are shown, with no charts. Of the 25 low-complexity 99215 claims on the card, some (C0034704, C0034724, C0034767) have documented high MDM and time, which the summary does not discuss as a tension with the low complexity of those patients.","The summary does not flag that 99215 charts were supported even for patients with few conditions, which weakens the upcoding signal. It also does not clearly separate the strong statistical anomaly from the weak documentation evidence."]}
